headline: PLS and GXAI hammered today while MSFT copped a big hit last night — a rough session across the board, but the RBA held rates steady which is good news for your mortgage.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara got smacked today, dropping 6.3% to $5.04. Lithium stocks have been on a rollercoaster — despite some recent buzz about a comeback, the broader lithium price outlook remains under pressure as supply continues to outpace demand. PLS is now down 25% on your total investment.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI fell 5% today to $17.53, dragged down by weakness in global AI and tech stocks. Microsoft's heavy fall last night (a key holding in AI-focused ETFs) weighed on sentiment across the sector. You're now down about 7% overall on this one.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dropped 3.5% last night to $352.83 — a notable fall. Reports suggest investors are reassessing the near-term returns on Microsoft's massive AI spending, even as analysts remain broadly bullish with near-unanimous 'buy' ratings. You're now down about 20% on your total MSFT investment.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE fell 2.4% today to $92.90. Emerging market stocks pulled back broadly, likely reflecting ongoing uncertainty around global growth and a softer risk appetite. You're slightly underwater on this one overall (-1.8%).

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS slipped 1.5% today to $523.20, reflecting last night's mild US market weakness — the NASDAQ dropped 0.46% and the S&P 500 was essentially flat. Still slightly in the green overall (+1.5%).

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG edged down 0.8% last night to $342.19 — a relatively modest move. Seeking Alpha called it 'the most explosive AI compounder' in a bullish piece out yesterday, so the dip appears to be broader market noise rather than company-specific bad news. Still up 11.3% overall.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped a modest 0.6% today to $76.54, tracking general softness in global markets. No specific news — this is just the diversified ETF moving with the tide. Still slightly in the green overall (+1.5%).

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL was the standout today, nudging up 0.9% to $8.10 — bucking the trend. This is a bit surprising given crude oil (WTI) actually fell 2.2% last night to $70.37/barrel. The ETF's slight gain may reflect currency moves or a lag in pricing energy stocks versus the spot oil price.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO rose 1.25% last night to $238.72 despite GTA 6 pre-order details reportedly disappointing some investors on price and launch specifics. The stock holding up suggests the market is still broadly confident in the GTA 6 launch story. You're up about 4% overall on this one.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Hold for now, but watch closely
watch_today.detail: Pilbara fell 6.3% today and is down 25% on your total investment. Lithium stocks are struggling with weak prices and oversupply globally. There's no clear catalyst to turn this around quickly — hold rather than add until there's a firmer sign of a lithium price recovery. Worth revisiting if it breaks below $5.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Hold despite the ugly session last night
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dropped 3.5% last night, pushing your position to a 20% overall loss. The cause appears to be investor nerves about the cost of Microsoft's AI buildout vs near-term returns. However, analysts remain almost universally bullish with 'strong buy' ratings. Hold — this looks like a sentiment wobble rather than a fundamental breakdown.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — Hold, but this needs watching
watch_today.detail: The AI ETF dropped 5% today and you're down 7% overall. The weakness is tied to broader tech selling — Microsoft's fall last night rippled through AI-exposed stocks. No news specific to GXAI, but if tech sentiment stays soft heading into next week, this could slide further. Hold for now.

watch_today.title: RBA held rates today — relief for borrowers
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank left interest rates on hold today, giving mortgage holders a reprieve. Economists are warning that underlying inflation (the 'core' measure that strips out volatile items) is still climbing, so rate hikes aren't completely off the table yet. Good for consumer sentiment and Australian equities in the near term.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 details out — TTWO still holding up
watch_today.detail: Rockstar released GTA 6 screenshots and pre-order details, with some commentators flagging the price and launch specifics as underwhelming. Despite the mixed reaction, TTWO rose 1.25% last night — the market seems to be giving Rockstar the benefit of the doubt. Hold and watch for any further detail on the release date.

watch_today.title: Crude oil sliding — headwind for FUEL.AX
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil dropped 2.2% last night to $70.37/barrel, and analysts suggest it could take time to recover to pre-war levels. FUEL.AX managed a small gain today despite this, but sustained low oil prices would eventually weigh on global energy company earnings. Hold but keep an eye on crude.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a quietly positive session today, closing up 0.18% at 8,764 — a modest gain against a mixed global backdrop. Last night on Wall Street, the NASDAQ slipped 0.46% and the S&P 500 was basically flat (-0.01%). The bigger stories were in individual stocks: Microsoft took a 3.5% hit. Gold continued its strong run, climbing 0.53% to $4,052/oz — a new high. Crude oil fell 2.2% to $70.37/barrel. The Aussie dollar is holding steady around US68.97 cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Modest gain today — held up well given broader tech weakness.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — investors in a wait-and-see mood.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Mild dip last night, dragged by Microsoft and broader tech softness.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell last night — analysts say a return to pre-war levels will take time.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold keeps climbing — investors seeking safety amid uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Barely moved — sitting just under US69 cents.

politics.summary: Big day in Australian domestic policy — the RBA held rates steady (good news for borrowers), Labor's major tax reforms passed parliament, and the government is tightening the social media ban for under-16s. Rate hike fears haven't fully gone away though, with economists pointing to rising underlying inflation.

stories.title: RBA holds interest rates steady — but economists warn hikes still possible
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank left rates on hold today, giving mortgage holders a breather. However, economists are flagging that underlying inflation — the 'core' measure that smooths out one-off price spikes — is still rising. Unemployment also dipped recently, which typically means the economy is running hot enough that the RBA might still need to raise rates. So while today's hold is good news, it's not all clear yet.

stories.title: Labor's $77 billion tax reforms pass parliament
stories.why_it_matters: Labor's major tax package — worth $77 billion — has cleared parliament. The Albanese government called it a win, but Pauline Hanson and the Coalition hit out at what they called 'lies' and 'dirty deals' to get the votes over the line. The reforms reshape who pays what in Australia, and Labor has been signalling it won't rule out further policy back-downs after its recent 'widow's tax' reversal on superannuation death benefit taxes.

stories.title: Government to strengthen social media ban for under-16s
stories.why_it_matters: Australia is toughening its world-first social media ban for children under 16. The government announced today it will strengthen the existing law — likely meaning stricter age verification requirements on platforms like TikTok, Instagram and X. This continues to put Australia at the front of global efforts to regulate kids' online access, and puts more pressure on tech giants to actually enforce the rules.

stories.title: Labor won't rule out more budget back-downs after 'widow's tax' U-turn
stories.why_it_matters: After caving on the 'widow's tax' — a proposed change to how superannuation death benefits are taxed that would have hit bereaved spouses — the Albanese government is now refusing to rule out further backflips on budget measures. This signals a more cautious, politically-sensitive approach to fiscal policy, which could mean less certainty for investors and superannuation holders about what's locked in versus what might change.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is Chinese models closing the gap on OpenAI and Anthropic — a shift that has real implications for US tech dominance. Locally, there's debate about whether Australia is doing enough on AI to lift productivity, while data centre cowboys are getting called out.

stories.title: Chinese AI models are catching up to OpenAI and Anthropic fast
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese AI companies are now producing models that benchmark close to — and in some cases match — OpenAI's GPT and Anthropic's Claude. This matters for US tech giants because it challenges the assumption that American companies have a durable lead in AI. For your holdings like GOOG (via Alphabet) and MSFT, increased competition from Chinese models could pressure margins on AI products and services down the track. It also adds to geopolitical uncertainty in the tech sector.

stories.title: CDC boss warns of data centre 'cowboys' amid AI gold rush
stories.why_it_matters: The boss of CDC Data Centres (one of Australia's biggest data centre operators) has publicly warned about dodgy operators flooding into the data centre market on the back of AI hype — calling them 'fly-by-night, cowboy-types.' The AI boom is driving massive demand for data centres, but not all new players have the experience or capital to deliver. This is worth watching for anyone invested in AI infrastructure plays.

stories.title: AI and regulatory reform key to lifting Australia's flat productivity — CommBank
stories.why_it_matters: CommBank's research arm argues that Australia's productivity growth — how much output we get per hour of work — has stalled, and that embracing AI alongside regulatory reform is the key fix. The argument is that if Australia doesn't lean into AI adoption in business and government, we'll fall further behind comparable economies. For investors, this is a signal that AI tailwinds in Australia are still in early innings.

stories.title: Leaked model names suggest a big month ahead: GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.5 Pro, Opus 4.8 and more
stories.why_it_matters: Leaked information suggests a wave of major AI model updates is coming in late June — reportedly including GPT-5.6 from OpenAI, Gemini 3.5 Pro from Google, Anthropic's Opus 4.8, and a mysterious model called 'Mythos 1.' If accurate, this would be one of the most competitive months in AI model releases ever. For your GOOG holding (Alphabet/Google), a strong Gemini release could be a positive catalyst. Keep an eye on any official announcements.

sport.summary: The Rabbitohs hammered the Eels last night in Round 17, the NRL is reportedly on the verge of a historic $5 billion broadcast deal, and Wimbledon kicks off with an Australian qualifier making headlines. In the AFL, Essendon has launched a formal coaching search and Michael Voss opened up about his struggles.

stories.title: Rabbitohs thrash Eels 32-12 — coach punches a wall
stories.why_it_matters: The Rabbitohs ran over the Eels 32-12 at CommBank Stadium last night in a Round 17 opener. Eels coach Brad Arthur (or his successor — reports describe a furious reaction post-game) reportedly punched a wall and bemoaned 'park football' from his side. Fox Sports described it as 'a really poor night in defence' for Parramatta. South Sydney look sharp heading into the back half of the season.

stories.title: NRL on the verge of a historic $5 billion broadcast deal
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL is reportedly close to locking in a mammoth $5 billion broadcast rights deal — which would be the biggest in the sport's history. If confirmed, this would dramatically increase the money flowing through the competition, potentially lifting player salaries, club revenues and the overall value of the NRL brand. The deal would likely cover several years of coverage across free-to-air and streaming platforms.

stories.title: Titans vs Bulldogs tonight on the Gold Coast — Round 17 continues
stories.why_it_matters: Round 17 continues tonight with two games — the Titans host the Bulldogs at Cbus Super Stadium at 6pm (your local ground on the Gold Coast), followed by the Broncos vs Roosters at Suncorp at 8pm. The Broncos-Roosters clash is shaping as one of the games of the round with both clubs in the top half of the ladder.

stories.title: Australian qualifier makes it to Wimbledon in 'incredibly special moment'
stories.why_it_matters: An Australian underdog has come through qualifying to earn a main draw spot at Wimbledon, which starts this week. The ABC described it as an 'incredibly special moment' for the player. Wimbledon's women's draw is being tipped as wide open this year, with no clear favourite according to the Australian Open's preview — meaning plenty of opportunity for upsets and storylines to follow.

stories.title: Essendon names panel to lead AFL senior coach search
stories.why_it_matters: Essendon has formally set up a panel to lead the search for their next senior AFL coach. The Bombers have been without a permanent appointment after their recent coaching change, and the formal search process signals the club is getting serious about finding the right person. The appointment will be one of the most watched coaching hires in the AFL given Essendon's large fanbase and the pressure on the club to return to finals.
